conventions.convention: Leakage is finite mutual information in natural-log nats; normalized block leakage is I(M;Z^n)/n.

The wiretap channel specifies a joint finite kernel W(y,z|x), whose coordinate product retains conditional Bob–Eve dependence. Codes have uniform messages, private encoder randomness, no feedback, no preshared secret key or forward public aid, and erasure counts as decoding error.
Degradation means the joint factorization W(y,z|x)=W_Y(y|x)V(z|y), rather than merely a relation between marginal channels.
Weak secrecy requires I(M_n;Z^n)/n→0; strong secrecy requires I(M_n;Z^n)→0, among reliable sequences.
Achievability uses one code at every integer blocklength n≥1, liminf rate at least R, and independently selected average/maximal-error and weak/strong-secrecy criteria.
Source releases factor as P_SXZ=P_SX K_Z|X. Privacy–utility coordinates are (I(S;Z), I(X;Z)), and the region takes the closure over finite release alphabets and kernels.
The leftover-hash distance is TV(P_KHZ,U_M⊗P_HZ), with TV equal to half the finite ℓ1 distance. The uniform hash seed is independent of (X,Z) and remains public; the conclusion is a TV guarantee.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite wiretap DMC with no input-cost constraint, feedback, or preshared secret key, all four average/maximal-error and weak/strong-secrecy capacities equal max[I(U;Y)−I(U;Z)] over finite U-X-(Y,Z); the maximum is attained with |U|≤|X|.

For a fixed finite DMC input law, R_0>I(U;Z), and 0<γ<R_0−I(U;Z), an IID codebook of ceil(exp(nR_0)) words has expected directional KL divergence at most exp(−n(R_0−I−γ))+(ln 2+nB)ρ^n and expected TV at most ρ^n+exp(−n(R_0−I−γ)/2)/2, for some 0<ρ<1.

Every finite auxiliary law P_UX is dominated in I(U;Y)−I(U;Z) by one with auxiliary alphabet size at most |X|. The auxiliary supremum is a maximum; the single-letter input objective is continuous on the finite simplex.
For a fixed finite DMC input law, supported information density J is bounded with mean I. Its IID sum satisfies Pr[|S_n/n−I|≥δ]≤σ²/(nδ²), and for every γ>0, Pr[S_n>n(I+γ)]≤ρ^n for some 0<ρ<1.

A finite wiretap channel is a stochastic joint kernel W(y,z|x) with coordinate-product block law; its code model specifies uniform messages, private randomized encoding, decoding with erasure, average/maximal error, and rate n^−1 ln|M_n|.
For a finite degraded wiretap channel, all four operational capacities equal max_PX[I(X;Y)−I(X;Z)], and this maximum is attained.
I(S;Z)=0 if and only if, for each positive-mass release value z, the mixture sum_x P(X=x|S=s)K(z|x) is independent of s over the support of P_S; zero-mass sensitive values are unconstrained.
For an independent uniform seed in a finite nonempty two-universal family with M outputs, TV(P_KHZ,U_M⊗P_HZ)≤sqrt(M g(X|Z))/2, where g(X|Z)=sum_z max_x P_XZ(x,z).

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite entropy, directional KL, zero-coordinate conventions, uniform entropy, and the binary example computations.
Natural logarithm and exponential inverse conventions in information density and concentration.
Differentiation of the finite exponential moment sum at zero in the information-density exponential-tail argument.
The substitution yielding ln(1+x)≤x for x≥0 in soft covering, and the endpoint entropy-continuity bound in the cardinality lemma.
Compactness of the nonempty closed bounded finite-dimensional weights-and-posteriors parameter space.
Attainment of the continuous auxiliary objective on that compact parameter space.

concerns.concern: Proof step 3.1 correctly selects an endpoint with G(t)≤G(0), but its explanation says: “otherwise zero, a convex combination of t_- and t_+, would have a larger value than both endpoints.” If neither endpoint satisfies the required inequality, G(0) would instead be smaller than both endpoint values, contradicting affinity. The word “larger” reverses this explanation; the endpoint inequality and subsequent support reduction are correct.

seams_checked.note: The finite DMC and stochastic product-law interfaces match the wiretap marginals and induced auxiliary channels. Fixed-input threshold reliability is proved locally; no stronger achievability assertion is attributed to the ordinary capacity theorem.

The prerequisite provides compatible finite-IID, positive-support, and nats context. The batch proves its information-density concentration directly and does not claim that the source AEP supplies the exponential tail needed for soft covering.

This is a contextual page prerequisite. The QKD definitions and sum-bound theorem use their own quantum trace-distance and abort-weighting conventions; they do not extend the classical leftover-hash theorem to quantum side information or identify mutual-information secrecy with composable security.
